newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Australia's Ampol cracker in uncheduled shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Ampol cracker in uncheduled shutdown.

text.p: Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol), the country's largest refiner, shut down a 22,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) at Kurnell on January 7 due to regenerator problems, a company source said on Friday.
"We tried cutting rates but it just "fell over"," the source said, referring to a failure to maintain the production of the FCC.
He said the unscheduled shutdown will continue until the end of the month.
There were no distillate shortages as these were being sourced from Ampol's other refinery at Lytton, near Brisbane which was running flat out, he said.
Ampol will go-ahead with its plans to shut down for maintenance its other 23,000-bpd FCC located at its 115,000-bpd Kurnell refinery, mid-February for three weeks, the company source said.
The refiner's only other scheduled turnaround is for a 40,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at the 100,000-bpd Lytton refinery in the fourth quarter.
A company spokesman said the timings and duration of the shutdowns have yet to be finalised.
Ampol is jointly owned by Pioneer International Ltd and Caltex Australia Ltd.
